tasks.q: In a client-server network, what does a client do?
a: Requests services, such as files or web pages, from a server
Provides services to every other computer
Connects the network to the internet
tasks.fb: Clients ask; servers provide. Connecting to the internet is the router's job.

tasks.q: Which of these is acting as a server?
a: A computer that stores students' files and checks their logins
A laptop being used to write an essay
tasks.fb: A server provides a service to other computers on the network.

tasks.q: What is a peer in a peer-to-peer network?
a: A computer that both requests and provides resources, as an equal
A computer that only requests services
tasks.fb: Peers act as both client and server, sharing directly with each other.

tasks.q: Who is responsible for backups in a peer-to-peer network?
a: Each user, for their own computer
tasks.fb: With no server, there's no central backup: every user has to manage their own.

tasks.q: Which is an advantage of a client-server network?
a: It is easier to take backups of all the shared data
It is cheaper to set up
There is no dependency on a single machine
tasks.fb: All the shared data is stored on the server, so one backup covers it. The other options describe peer-to-peer.

tasks.q: Why is the server a single point of failure?
a: If it stops working, the clients can't reach the files and services it provides
Only one person can log in at a time
It can only store one file
It has only one network cable
tasks.fb: Everything depends on the server, so a server failure affects every client.

tasks.q: Which is a disadvantage of peer-to-peer?
a: Users need to manage their own backups
The server is a single point of failure
tasks.fb: The other three are disadvantages of client-server.

tasks.q: Why is peer-to-peer usually cheaper to set up?
a: No expensive server hardware is needed
It only works with one computer
tasks.fb: The peers are ordinary computers, so there's no server to buy or specialist to pay.

tasks.q: Match each role to what it does.
pairs: Provides services and resources to other computers
Both requests and provides resources, as an equal
tasks.fb: These are the definitions to learn for the exam.

tasks.q: A games console downloads an update from the manufacturer's server. What is the console?
tasks.fb: The console requests the update, so it is the client.

tasks.q: Torrenting is an example of which model?
tasks.fb: Every user's computer shares pieces directly with the others, so they act as peers.

tasks.q: Why can torrent downloads be fast?
a: Pieces come from many peers at the same time, so no single server limits the speed
Only one person can download at once
tasks.fb: Lots of peers each sending a piece adds up to a fast download, especially for popular files.

tasks.q: Does each statement describe client-server or peer-to-peer?
items: Each user has to back up their own machine
Files end up scattered and hard to find
No expensive central machine to buy
One nightly backup covers everyone's shared work
Carries on working if one computer is switched off
Security settings are hard to apply consistently
Needs trained staff to look after it
New software can be pushed to every machine at once
Costs more to buy and to run
Anyone can set it up without training
Everything stops if the central machine fails
tasks.fb: Now mark each statement on your worksheet: is it an advantage or a disadvantage?

info.title: Virtual servers
info.text: One powerful physical computer can run many virtual servers at once, each acting as a separate server. Most school and cloud servers work this way.

info.title: Napster
info.text: In 1999, Napster made peer-to-peer music sharing famous. It was shut down in 2001 after legal action, because most of the music was shared without permission.

info.title: Server rooms
info.text: Servers are kept in locked, air-conditioned rooms, often with backup power supplies, because a server failure affects everyone.

info.title: P2P is legal
info.text: Peer-to-peer technology is completely legal. What's illegal is sharing copyrighted films, music or games without permission.

info.title: Online games
info.text: Most online games use dedicated servers. Some older games used peer-to-peer, where one player's console hosted the match for everyone.

info.title: Updates from peers
info.text: Some operating systems can download pieces of an update from other computers on your network, peer-to-peer, instead of all from the maker's servers.
